title: NOFIS: Normalizing Flow for Rare Circuit Failure Analysis
problem: Conventional Monte Carlo methods for estimating rare IC failure probability are inefficient, requiring exorbitant sample sizes. Accurate rare failure probability estimation is essential yet challenging for ensuring circuit reliability.
motivation: Accurate rare failure probability estimation is crucial for ensuring the proper and reliable functioning of integrated circuits.
method: NOFIS learns a sequence of proposal distributions for predefined nested subset events by minimizing KL divergence losses, leveraging normalizing flows' exact sampling capabilities. It then estimates rare event probability using importance sampling with the learned final proposal distribution.
key_novelty: Using normalizing flows to learn optimal proposal distributions for importance sampling to efficiently estimate rare circuit failure probabilities.
contributions: NOFIS method combining normalizing flows with importance sampling for rare event probability estimation
Learning sequence of proposal distributions via KL divergence minimization for nested subset events
Superior accuracy over baseline Monte Carlo approaches demonstrated across 10 quantitative experiments
